newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold closes firmer in two-way trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold closes firmer in two-way trading.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended up from the New York close on early short-covering despite late profit-taking in narrow two-way Tuesday trading, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$362.20/70 an ounce against New York's US$361.70/362.20 close on Monday.
"Early short-covering boosted gold to a day high of US$382.60/363.10, but profit-taking depressed the price in late trade," said a dealer at an international metals house.
"Sentiment is mixed in the immediate future and I think gold will stay range-bound, with downside support at US$360 and upside resistance at US$365, then $368."
Local gold ended HK$1 lower at HK$3,353 a tael.
The carry over charge per 10 taels of gold at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped slightly to +4.00 from +5.00 at its previous fix.
